implementation_notes: In .NET the classic scatter is the contract: a field added to a domain type propagates through the DTO, the AutoMapper profile, the interface, the view model and the test builder. The cure is to decide which of those are genuinely part of the contract — usually the DTO and the interface — and to generate or map the rest, or to expose fewer types. C# 9's `init` accessors and `record` types reduce the boilerplate but not the scatter, which is why the check that matters is 'which types are part of the published contract' rather than 'which properties exist'.
idiom_name: one change across DTO, mapper, view model and interface
pitfalls: AutoMapper profiles are the hidden fourth site: a property silently stops being mapped and nobody sees it until a test fails.
Interfaces with many members mean every implementation changes when the contract grows — which is exactly the signal that the interface is the god object of the subsystem.
`partial` classes across files let one type hide a scatter that the file listing does not reveal.
